So prompt engineering is gone and Loop engineering is the new thing you need to learn.

What is Loop Engineering?
It's a system where you write loops instead of single prompts. A loop is a goal AI keeps working towards until it gets there. It plans, executes, checks its result against set expectations and feeds the result back in and goes again.

There are five parts in any loop: discover, plan, execute, verify, iterate

The verifier is the most important since this is what sets the explicit expectations.

For example:

Goal: One LinkedIn post on "why shorter AI prompts win."

Loop:
1. DRAFT the post.
2. Switch roles: you're now a strict editor who didn't write it.
 Score pass/fail:
 (a) hook is under 12 words
 (b) has one specific number or example
 (c) zero cliches like "game changer" or "the future is here"
 (d) ends with a question, not a summary
3. Any fail -> rewrite and re-score.

Stop: all 4 pass, or 3 rounds max. Show every scorecard + final post.

If you’re in your 20s, read this: 

You live as if you were destined to live forever, no thought of your frailty ever enters your head, of how much time has already gone by you take no heed. You squander time as if you drew from a full and abundant supply. 

But for a man, the age of 25 is not just a passing year. It is the axis upon which the rest of his life turns. It is the moment of reckoning, a crossroads that demands a choice; Will you dare to pursue greatness, a path strewn with suffering, sacrifice, and isolation? Or will you choose comfort, the path of mediocrity, where pleasure comes easily but significance fades like mist in the morning sun?

Each choice carries its own form of suffering. If you choose greatness, you must endure the quiet torment of discipline, the weight of unrealised dreams pressing against your chest like an iron vice. If you choose mediocrity, you must live with the slow erosion of your soul, the quiet agony of irrelevance, as the world moves forward and you remain still, unnoticed.

So, if you must suffer—and you must—why not suffer for something meaningful? Why not let the pain become a chisel, carving the raw stone of your existence into something worthy of remembrance? Learn to love the weight of it, for it will become your proof of life.

And when the world becomes too gentle, too seductive, and whispers its false promises of ease and pleasure, remind yourself of this:

“The woods are lovely, dark and deep,
But I have promises to keep,
And miles to go before I sleep,
And miles to go before I sleep.”
Been Steel. Still Steel.
